description_full: Telefônica Brasil S.A., together with its subsidiaries, operates as a mobile telecommunications company in Brazil. Its fixed line voice services portfolio includes local, domestic long-distance, and international long-distance calls; and mobile portfolio comprises voice and broadband internet access through 3G, 4G, 4.5G, and 5G, as well as value-added, prepaid plans with data sharing features, family plans, voice mail, caller identification, voice minutes in unlimited bundles to mobile and fixed-line phones, and digital services, and wireless roaming services. The company also offers data services, including broadband and mobile data services; fixed-line local services consist of activation, monthly subscription, public telephones and measured services. In addition, it provides pay TV services through IPTV technologies; network services, such as rental of facilities and other services; wholesale services, including interconnection services to users of other network providers; and digital services that include entertainment, cloud, and security and financial services. Further, the company offers multimedia communication services, which include audio, data, voice and other sounds, images, texts, and other information, as well as sells devices and accessories, such as smartphones, broadband USB modems, and other devices. Additionally, it provides telecommunications solutions and IT support to various industries, such as retail, manufacturing, services, financial institutions, government, etc; insurance services; and sale of wireless devices and consumer electronics. It markets and sells its solutions through Vivo stores, dealers, retail channels, distribution and digital channels, door-to-door sales, and outbound tele sales. The company was formerly known as Telecomunicações de São Paulo S.A. - TELESP and changed its name to Telefônica Brasil S.A. in October 2011. Telefônica Brasil S.A. was incorporated in 1998 and is headquartered in São Paulo, Brazil.

financial_summary: Telefonica Brasil S.A. is a large-cap communication services business with a $18.3B market cap.
Returns on capital run at 9% against a 8% cost of capital, which means the business barely earns its keep economically.
The business throws off $2.0B in free cash flow, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 3.35× so those profits are backed by real cash.
Accruals are elevated at -11.4% of assets, and Sloan showed firms building earnings through accruals rather than cash systematically underperform.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 0.5× net debt/EBITDA, and thin 2.2× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.

Shareholder yield of 3.9% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome.

sect: Over five years it has been losing share of the sector profit pool (-7.6% a year).
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.06 across 169 companies in the universe; the top four hold 36% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares have drifted higher, up 7% over the past year excluding the latest month.
The price sits near the bottom of its 52-week range, 34% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 34% and a beta of 0.50, it is more defensive than the market.
About $16.1M trades a day, enough to build a position, and interest is running hot at 1.5x its yearly average volume.
In past sell-offs it fell 46% in the 2020 crash, 39% in the 2022 bear market and 41% in 2008.
val: The stock trades 68% below its DCF fair value of $35.36, a meaningful margin of safety.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 40%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $27.93 to $46.21 (P10-P90), so treat the estimate as noisy.
On multiples it looks cheap against Communication Services peers: EV/EBITDA 1.5 vs 9.4 and P/FCF 8.9 vs 11.3 (sector median).
Against its own history it is dear: the EBIT multiple sits 30% above its 10-year median.
Earnings yields are mixed: an FCF yield of 11.2% (above the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 6.1% (vs the 8% bar).
The 8 covering analysts target $13.95 on average, 22% above the price, well away from the model's fair value.
prof: ROIC of 9% earns above the cost of capital of 8.2%, but the 1pp spread is short of the 7pp moat bar; returns have been steady (CV 0.20).
Earnings quality is mixed: cash conversion of 3.35x, but high accruals (-11.4% of assets).
hlth: Leverage is conservative at 0.5x net debt to EBITDA ($1.3B of cash against $3.7B of debt), and interest cover is thin at 2.2x.
Warning signs: an Altman Z of 1.27 in the distress zone, which caps the rating at HOLD.
The current ratio of 1.00 means short-term liabilities exceed current assets.
growth: Net reinvestment is nil (capex and working capital no more than cover depreciation), so fundamental growth is near zero.
Free cash flow has compounded -1.4% a year over five years, short of the 5% durability bar.
It has missed earnings estimates by 17.2% on average.
Analysts expect 11.8% long-term annual earnings growth.
own: Insiders hold little stock (0.0%), and institutions hold 4%.
It returns 3.9% a year to shareholders (1.7% in buybacks and 8.8% in dividends).
The share count has grown 13.6% a year over five years, diluting existing holders.
It pays out 120% of earnings, more than it earns, so the dividend is at risk.
